records.rationale: Defines `legacyIds` on `devcontainer-feature.json`, a Feature-authoring metadata property. Its schema twins (cst-feature-*/legacyIds, property-existence and type) are classified not-applicable for the same reason: deacon consumes published Features and never authors, validates or publishes them (constitution II).

Defines `deprecated` on `devcontainer-feature.json`, a Feature-authoring metadata property whose schema twins (cst-feature-*/deprecated) are classified not-applicable. Deprecation is a signal to authors and registries; deacon installs a published Feature regardless of the flag and emits no deprecation surface. Out of consumer-only scope.

Restates the meaning of the authoring-metadata `deprecated` flag and confirms that existing configurations keep working because the OCI artifacts remain. The obligation is on the publisher, not on the consumer; deacon's install path is unchanged by the flag. Out of consumer-only scope.

Describes a planned change to the reference tooling so that `installsAfter` also matches a Feature's authoring-declared `legacyIds`. It bites only for a renamed published Feature referenced by its old id, and the property it keys on is the same authoring metadata whose schema twins are not-applicable; deacon models no `legacyIds` field (no occurrence in crates/core or crates/deacon) and resolves order by the identifier the author wrote. Out of consumer-only scope, on the authoring side of the rename workflow.

States the motivation for the authoring-metadata `legacyIds` property (renaming a published Feature within one namespace). Renaming and republishing are Feature-authoring workflows deacon has no command for. Out of consumer-only scope.

Versioning guidance addressed to the Feature author across a rename (continue the semver line, do not restart at 1.0.0). It constrains what an author publishes, never what a consumer does with what is published. Out of consumer-only scope (constitution II).

Describes what the publishing command does with `legacyIds` (dual-publish the old and new ids). `features publish` is permanently out of deacon's scope (constitution II); deacon only resolves and installs already-published Features.
